abschnitte.text: Jesus was on his way to **Jerusalem** with his disciples. He sent two disciples to a village. There they were to find a young **donkey** tied up, on which, according to **Mark**, no one had ever sat. The disciples **untied it** and brought it to Jesus. They laid their cloaks on the donkey, and Jesus sat on it.

Jesus came from the **Mount of Olives**, which lies east of Jerusalem. Many people spread their **clothes** and **branches** on the road. That was how a king was welcomed at the time. They shouted “**Hosanna**” and praised Jesus. Some **Pharisees** wanted Jesus to silence the crowd. Jesus answered that then the **stones would cry out**.

At that time a **horse** was an animal for war. But Jesus rode on a **donkey**, a simple and peaceful mount. In this way he showed that he comes as a **king of peace**. The Gospels see in this the fulfilment of a prophet's word from the Book of Zechariah. According to **Luke**, Jesus wept when he saw the city before him, because he knew that hard times were coming for it.

In Jerusalem Jesus went into the **Temple**. There people were trading and changing money. Jesus overturned the tables of the traders and **drove them out**. He said that God's house should be a **house of prayer**. This story is also called the **cleansing of the Temple**.

Christians remember the entry on **Palm Sunday**, the Sunday before Easter. With it **Holy Week** begins. According to the Gospel of John, the branches on the road were palm branches, hence the name. In many Catholic congregations in Switzerland, **palm bunches** of branches are blessed on this day. Some churches also hold a procession.

gewusst: “Hosanna” comes from Hebrew and was originally a cry for help, later a cry of joy.
In some places, a wooden donkey with a figure of Jesus used to be pulled through the streets, the Palmesel.

teile.einleitung: Trinity Sunday is a Christian feast one week after Pentecost. It celebrates the belief in one God in three persons: Father, Son and Holy Spirit. In Protestant churches it is often called Trinitatis.
wichtigste: Trinity Sunday is the Sunday after Pentecost.
God is celebrated as Father, Son and Holy Spirit.
In Protestant churches the feast is called Trinitatis, from the Latin “trinitas”, threefoldness.
Pope John XXII prescribed the feast for the whole Church in 1334.
A common symbol is the triangle.
Saint Patrick is said to have explained the Trinity with a shamrock.

abschnitte.text: **Trinity Sunday** follows one week after **Pentecost**. With it the Easter season comes to an end. Because Easter is on a different date every year, this feast moves too. It always falls in May or June. A few days later, on the Thursday, Catholics celebrate **Corpus Christi**.

Christians believe in **one God** who shows himself as **Father**, **Son** and **Holy Spirit**. This teaching is called the **Trinity**. It is not easy to understand, which is why there are many images for it. An important basis is the **baptismal command** in the Gospel of Matthew, chapter 28, verse 19. There Jesus sends out the disciples to baptise in the name of the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit.

In some regions the feast was already celebrated in the early Middle Ages. It was prescribed for the whole Church by Pope **John XXII** in the year **1334**. In **Protestant churches** the day is called **Trinitatis**, from the Latin word “trinitas”, threefoldness. The following Sundays there are counted as “Sundays after Trinity” until the autumn.

A common symbol is the equilateral **triangle**, often with an eye in it. Its three equal sides together form one unity. According to legend, Saint **Patrick** explained the Trinity to the people of **Ireland** with a **shamrock**: three leaves and yet one plant. That is why the shamrock is a symbol of Ireland today.

gewusst: In many places in Austria and southern Germany, Trinity columns stand in the squares.
The eye in the triangle can also be found on the back of the American one-dollar note.

teile.einleitung: Hesychasm is a form of prayer in the **Orthodox Church**. The name comes from the Greek word **hesychia**, which means stillness. The Hesychasts seek closeness to God in inner quiet and with the Jesus Prayer.
wichtigste: Hesychia means stillness in Greek.
Hesychasts repeat the Jesus Prayer without ceasing.
Gregory Palamas defended Hesychasm in the 14th century.
His opponent was Barlaam of Calabria.
Palamas distinguished between God's essence and God's energies.
The Philokalia appeared in Venice in 1782.

abschnitte.text: The Hesychasts strive for **inner stillness** in order to meet God. For this they repeat the **Jesus Prayer** without ceasing. It usually goes: “Lord Jesus Christ, Son of God, have mercy on me.” The prayer is often linked with the **breath** and counted on a prayer rope. This form of prayer is especially cultivated by monks on **Mount Athos** in Greece.

In the 14th century the scholar **Barlaam of Calabria** from southern Italy sharply criticised the Hesychasts. He thought it impossible to really see God, and mocked their method of prayer. The monk **Gregory Palamas** defended Hesychasm. He was a monk on Athos and later Archbishop of **Thessalonica**. Synods in Constantinople confirmed his teaching.

abschnitte.titel: Essence, energies and the Taboric light
abschnitte.text: At the centre of Palamas's teaching is a distinction: God's **essence** remains unknowable to human beings, but God's **energies** can be experienced. The Hesychasts believed that in prayer they could behold the **Taboric light**. This means the light that the disciples saw at the Transfiguration of Jesus on Mount Tabor. This light is regarded as an effect of God, not as his essence.

In 1782 the **Philokalia** appeared in **Venice**, a collection of texts on inner prayer. The name means “love of the beautiful”. It was compiled by Nikodemos of the Holy Mountain and Makarios of Corinth. The collection spread Hesychasm especially in **Russia**. To this day many Orthodox Christians read in it.

gewusst: The Jesus Prayer is also called the prayer of the heart.
Some Christians in Western churches also pray the Jesus Prayer today.

teile.einleitung: The biblical canon is the list of writings that belong to the Bible. This list did not arise all at once but grew over centuries. Jews, Catholics and Protestants count the books in partly different ways.
wichtigste: The Greek word “canon” originally means guideline or yardstick.
The Hebrew Bible is called the Tanakh and consists of the Torah, Nevi'im and Ketuvim.
By the Jewish count the Tanakh comprises 24 books.
In the year 367 Athanasius of Alexandria named exactly the 27 writings of the New Testament.
The Council of Trent fixed the Catholic canon in 1546.
Luther called the Letter of James “an epistle of straw”.

abschnitte.text: The Greek word **canon** originally means **guideline** or **yardstick**. In the Church it describes the list of writings that count as Holy Scripture. These books are binding for faith. For a long time it was not entirely clear which writings belong to it. In the first centuries there was a lot of discussion about this.

The **Hebrew Bible** is called the **Tanakh**. The word is made up of the initial letters of its three parts: **Torah** (instruction), **Nevi'im** (prophets) and **Ketuvim** (writings). By the Jewish count the Tanakh comprises **24 books**. Christians call these writings the Old Testament, but count them differently, so that more books come out.

Around **AD 144**, **Marcion** created a collection of his own from a shortened Gospel of Luke and ten letters of Paul. He rejected the Old Testament. The Church rejected his teaching and thought harder about the canon. An early Latin list is the **Muratorian Fragment**, named after its discoverer. In the year **367**, **Athanasius of Alexandria** named for the first time, in an Easter letter, exactly the **27 writings** of the present-day New Testament.

The church historian **Eusebius of Caesarea** distinguished between accepted and disputed writings. The disputed ones he called **Antilegomena**. Doubts arose later too: in 1522 **Martin Luther** described the **Letter of James** as “an epistle of straw”. He found that this letter spoke too little of Christ. Even so, the letter stayed in his Bible.

The Catholic Church counts some books as part of the Old Testament that are not in the Tanakh, such as **Tobit** and **Judith**. The **Council of Trent** fixed this canon as binding in **1546**. For the Old Testament the Protestant churches follow the Hebrew extent. The additional books they call the **Apocrypha**, while Catholics speak of deuterocanonical books.

gewusst: The New Testament has the same 27 writings for Catholics, Orthodox and Protestants.
In his Bible, Luther put the Apocrypha in an appendix of their own between the Old and New Testaments.

teile.einleitung: Hildegard of Bingen was a nun, scholar and composer of the Middle Ages. She lived in the 12th century as a **Benedictine** on the Rhine. To this day she is known for her knowledge of nature and healing, her music and her visions.
wichtigste: Hildegard belonged to the order of the Benedictine nuns.
She was the tenth child of her parents.
At the age of eight she was brought up by Jutta of Sponheim.
Around 1150 she founded the convent of Rupertsberg near Bingen on the Rhine.
In her book “Scivias” she described her visions.
In 2012 Pope Benedict XVI declared her a Doctor of the Church.

abschnitte.text: Hildegard was born in 1098 as the **tenth child** of her parents. At the age of **eight** she was entrusted to the devout **Jutta of Sponheim** to be brought up. With her she learned to read, to pray and to sing the Psalms. Later Hildegard became a **Benedictine**. After Jutta's death she became the head of the community of women.

Around **1150** Hildegard founded the convent of **Rupertsberg** near Bingen. The town of **Bingen** lies on the **Rhine** in Germany. Later she also founded a second convent in Eibingen. Hildegard wrote letters to popes, emperors and bishops. For a woman in the Middle Ages she thereby had unusually great influence.

Today Hildegard is especially known for her knowledge of **nature and healing**. She described many plants, animals and stones and their effects. In doing so she combined the knowledge of her time with faith. To this day there are books and recipes that appeal to Hildegard. But not all of them really come from her.

abschnitte.titel: Visions, music and a secret language
abschnitte.text: In her book **“Scivias”** Hildegard described her **visions**, that is, images that, by her own account, she received from God. She also composed many songs and the sacred musical play **“Ordo Virtutum”**. With the **“Lingua ignota”** she invented her own **secret language** with many new words. In **2012** Pope Benedict XVI gave her the title **Doctor of the Church**.

gewusst: Hildegard is one of the first women composers whose names and works we know.
She lived to be about 81 years old, which was very unusual in the Middle Ages.

teile.einleitung: In South Korea, Christianity plays a large role. The Catholic Church came into being there in an unusual way, without missionaries. Today South Korea has many Protestants and some of the largest congregations in the world.
wichtigste: The Catholic Church in Korea was founded in the 18th century by lay people without missionaries.
Andrew Kim Taegon was the first Korean Catholic priest.
In 1984 Pope John Paul II declared 103 Korean martyrs saints in Seoul.
In 1885 the missionaries Underwood and Appenzeller arrived as Protestant pioneers.
According to the 2015 census, Protestants were the largest religious community.
The Yoido Full Gospel Church in Seoul is regarded as the largest single Pentecostal congregation in the world.

abschnitte.text: In the 18th century, Korean scholars read Christian books that came from China. They studied them and began to live the faith themselves. In this way the Catholic Church in Korea was founded by **lay people without missionaries**. This is something special in the history of the Church. Priests only came to the country later.

The rulers of Korea saw the new faith as a danger. In the 19th century many Christians were persecuted and killed. Among them was **Andrew Kim Taegon**, the **first Korean Catholic priest**. He died in 1846. In **1984**, during a visit to Seoul, Pope **John Paul II** declared **103** Korean martyrs saints, including Andrew Kim Taegon.

In **1885** the two American missionaries **Underwood** and **Appenzeller** came to Korea. They are regarded as pioneers of the Protestant churches there. They founded schools and helped to build hospitals. Protestantism then grew strongly. According to the South Korean census of **2015**, **Protestants** were the largest religious community, ahead of Buddhists and Catholics.

In the capital **Seoul** there are many churches, and at night red crosses glow on some rooftops. The **Yoido Full Gospel Church** is regarded as the **largest single Pentecostal congregation in the world**. The bishop's church of the Catholic Archdiocese of Seoul is the **Myeongdong Cathedral**. It was built of brick in the Gothic style at the end of the 19th century.

gewusst: In the 2015 census, more than half of the people in South Korea said they did not belong to any religion.
Pope Francis visited South Korea in 2014.

teile.einleitung: The Three Kings are the wise men from the East who, according to the Bible, visited the infant Jesus. Their feast is **Epiphany on 6 January**. In Switzerland it comes with the Three Kings' cake, which has a hidden king.
wichtigste: According to the Bible, the wise men came from the East.
They knelt before the child and brought three gifts.
People speak of three kings because there were three gifts.
A dream warned them not to return to King Herod.
Epiphany is on 6 January.
Carol singers write C+M+B and the year on doors.

abschnitte.titel: The wise men from the East
abschnitte.text: The **Gospel of Matthew** says that wise men from the **East** came to Jerusalem. They had followed a **star** and were looking for the newborn king of the Jews. The star led them to Bethlehem. When they found the child, they **knelt down** and honoured him. In many pictures they ride on **camels**, which can go a long time without water.

The wise men brought **gold**, **frankincense** and **myrrh**. **Frankincense** is the dried resin of a tree and smells sweet when burned. Myrrh too is a fragrant resin. The Bible does not say how many wise men there were. Because **three gifts** are mentioned, people imagined three visitors and later made them into kings.

King **Herod** had asked the wise men to tell him where the child was. But he did not want to honour the new king, he wanted to get rid of him. The wise men, however, were **warned in a dream**. So they travelled home by a different route. Later they were given the names Caspar, Melchior and Balthasar.

abschnitte.titel: Star singers and the Three Kings' cake
abschnitte.text: On **6 January** **Epiphany**, or Three Kings' Day, is celebrated; the Church also calls the feast Epiphany. Around this time **star singers** dressed as kings go from house to house and collect money for children in need. With chalk they write **C+M+B** and the year on the door. This stands for “Christus mansionem benedicat”, “May Christ bless this house”. In Switzerland people eat the **Three Kings' cake**, and whoever finds the hidden king may be king for a day.

gewusst: In Cologne Cathedral stands the Shrine of the Three Kings, in which, according to tradition, relics of the wise men lie.
The letters C, M and B are often also read as the initials of Caspar, Melchior and Balthasar.

teile.einleitung: The Armenian Apostolic Church is one of the oldest Christian churches in the world. According to tradition, Armenia became the first Christian state in the year 301. The Church has its own customs and its own script for its Bible.
wichtigste: According to tradition, King Tiridates III made Armenia a Christian state in 301.
Gregory the Illuminator is regarded as the missionary of Armenia and its first Catholicos.
The seat of the Catholicos of All Armenians is Etchmiadzin.
The Church belongs to the Oriental Orthodox churches.
Mesrop Mashtots created the Armenian alphabet around 405.
The Church traces itself back to the apostles Thaddaeus and Bartholomew.
It celebrates Christmas on 6 January.

abschnitte.text: According to tradition, the apostles **Thaddaeus** and **Bartholomew** already preached in Armenia in the 1st century. That is why the Church calls itself **“apostolic”**. According to tradition, King **Tiridates III** raised Christianity to the state religion in the year **301**. Armenia would thus be the **first Christian state** in the world. Some scholars date this rather to the year 314.

**Gregory the Illuminator** is regarded as the missionary of Armenia. He is said to have been held prisoner in a pit for years. Then he healed the king and converted him to Christianity. Gregory became the first **Catholicos**, as the head of the Church is called. The Church is sometimes also called **“Gregorian”** after him.

The seat of the **Catholicos of All Armenians** is **Etchmiadzin**, west of the capital **Yerevan**. The cathedral of Etchmiadzin is regarded as one of the oldest cathedrals in the world. There is also the **Catholicosate of the Great House of Cilicia**. It arose in the medieval kingdom of Cilicia and has had its seat in **Antelias** near Beirut in Lebanon since **1930**.

Around the year **405**, **Mesrop Mashtots** created the **Armenian alphabet**. He wanted the Armenians to be able to read the Bible in their own language. The Catholicos **Sahak** helped him. Soon afterwards the Armenian translation of the Bible was made. The alphabet is still used today and is an important part of Armenian culture.

abschnitte.titel: A church family of its own
abschnitte.text: Like the **Coptic** and the **Ethiopian** churches, the Armenian Church did not recognise the **Council of Chalcedon** of **451**. That is why it belongs to the **Oriental Orthodox churches**. It has kept an old custom: it celebrates the birth and the baptism of Jesus together on **6 January**. The Patriarchate in Jerusalem follows the Julian calendar and therefore celebrates on 19 January.

gewusst: There are Armenian congregations in Switzerland too, with a church in Troinex near Geneva.
Many Armenians live outside Armenia, for example in Russia, France and the USA.

teile.einleitung: Disciples are people who followed Jesus and learned from him. Jesus chose twelve of them as his innermost circle. They are also called apostles and were later to carry the message of Jesus into the world.
wichtigste: The word “disciple” means pupil.
Jesus called his first disciples at the Sea of Galilee.
The fishermen Simon Peter and Andrew left their nets behind.
James and John, the sons of Zebedee, also followed Jesus.
Matthew had been a tax collector.
The twelve closest disciples are called apostles.
Judas Iscariot betrayed Jesus, and later Matthias was chosen as the twelfth apostle.

abschnitte.text: The word **disciple** means **pupil**. A disciple accompanies his teacher, listens to him and lives as he teaches. Jesus had many disciples, men and also women. From them he chose **twelve** as his innermost circle. These Twelve are called the **apostles**, which means “those sent out”.

Jesus was walking along the shore of the **Sea of Galilee** in Galilee. There he saw the brothers **Simon Peter** and **Andrew**, who worked as fishermen. He called them to follow him, and they **left their nets behind**. After that he also called **James and John**, the sons of Zebedee. According to the Gospel of John, Andrew had previously been a pupil of **John the Baptist**.

abschnitte.titel: A tax collector becomes a disciple
abschnitte.text: Not all the disciples were fishermen. **Matthew** was a **tax collector**, so he collected customs duties and levies. Tax collectors were unpopular with many people at the time, because they worked for the Romans and often demanded too much. Jesus called Matthew all the same, and he followed him at once. The story shows that Jesus also accepted people whom others rejected.

One of the Twelve, **Judas Iscariot**, betrayed Jesus to his opponents. After the death and resurrection of Jesus an apostle was therefore missing. The Acts of the Apostles tells that the disciples chose a new one by **lot**: **Matthias**. Later the apostles went to many countries and told people about Jesus. In this way Christianity spread.

gewusst: Simon was given the surname **Peter** by Jesus, which means “rock”.
Many churches and places are named after apostles, for example the Cathedral of St Peter in Geneva.

teile.einleitung: A hymn book is a book of **songs for church services**. So that everyone can sing together, it is available in many churches. Alongside the words there is often also the musical notation of the tune.
wichtigste: The hymn book contains the songs for the service.
Every hymn has a number, so you can find it quickly.
The hymn numbers are shown at the front on a hymn board.
Songs for the service are called church hymns.
The musical notes are often above the words.
The hymn books are usually available in the pews.

abschnitte.titel: What is in the hymn book
abschnitte.text: A hymn book contains many **church hymns**, that is, songs sung in the service. Some are already several hundred years old, others are quite new. Often the **notes** are above the words, so you can see how the tune goes. Many hymn books also contain prayers and texts from the Bible. The songs are usually arranged by church year or by theme.

Every hymn has its own **number** in the hymn book. At the front of the church hangs a **hymn board**. Before the service the numbers of the hymns are put up there. That way everyone knows straight away which page to turn to. The hymn books are often available in the **church pews** or at the entrance and are put back afterwards.

Even in the Bible there is a book of songs: the **Psalms**. There are 150 songs and prayers. Many of them are attributed to **King David**, who is said to have loved playing the harp. In the Reformed churches, Psalms used to be sung especially often, for example in the Geneva Psalter.

Since the **Reformation**, the whole congregation has sung along in the service, not just a choir. For this, books with songs for everyone were needed. In German-speaking Switzerland today there are, for example, the **Reformed Hymn Book** and the **Catholic Hymn Book**. Many songs are in both books, because they are sung by all Christians.

gewusst: Some church hymns that are still sung today were written by Martin Luther and are almost 500 years old.
The invention of printing first made it possible for many people to have their own hymn book.

teile.einleitung: The Anglican Church came into being in England when the Church separated from Rome in the 16th century. Its mother church is the Church of England. Today there are Anglican churches on all continents.
wichtigste: King Henry VIII separated the Church of England from Rome in 1534.
The British monarch is formally the secular head of the Church of England.
The most important clergyman is the Archbishop of Canterbury.
The well-known prayer book is called the Book of Common Prayer.
British kings are crowned in Westminster Abbey.
In the USA the Anglican church is called the Episcopal Church.
The worldwide union is called the Anglican Communion.

abschnitte.text: King **Henry VIII** of England wanted to have his marriage annulled. The **pope** refused. The king then separated the Church of England from Rome. With the **Act of Supremacy** of **1534** he made himself the head of the Church of England. In this way the **Church of England** came into being.

Since the Reformation the **king** or **queen** has formally stood at the head of the Church of England. The title is **Supreme Governor**. In 2026 this is King **Charles III**. The most important clergyman, however, is the **Archbishop of Canterbury**. He is the highest-ranking bishop of the Church of England and is regarded as the spiritual centre of Anglicans worldwide.

The famous prayer book of the Anglicans is called the **Book of Common Prayer**. It first appeared in **1549** and goes back to Archbishop **Thomas Cranmer**. It brought worship in the **English language** instead of Latin. Many prayers from it are still well known in English today. The Anglican Church combines Catholic traditions with ideas of the Reformation.

In **Westminster Abbey** in London, British kings have been crowned since **1066**. The abbey is an Anglican church. King **Charles III** was also crowned there in **2023**. In Westminster Abbey many kings and famous figures are also buried.

The worldwide union of Anglican churches is called the **Anglican Communion**. It unites 42 independent church provinces and further churches on all continents. Many of them arose in former **British colonies**, for example in Africa. In the **USA** the Anglicans call themselves the **Episcopal Church**, because they are led by bishops. The Latin word for bishops is “episcopi”.

gewusst: In Switzerland too there are Anglican congregations with services in English, for example in Zurich, Bern and Geneva.
In the Church of England, priests may marry, and since 2014 women can also become bishops.

teile.einleitung: Ordination of women means that women are appointed to a spiritual office, for example as a pastor or priest. The churches handle this very differently. In Switzerland the first women pastors existed as early as 1918.
wichtigste: “Ordination” is the appointment to a spiritual office.
In 1918 the first women in Switzerland were ordained as pastors in Zurich.
Since 1963 women in the Reformed church of Zurich have been allowed to work fully as pastors.
In 1994 John Paul II declared that the Church could not ordain women as priests.
Since 2000 the Christ Catholic Church has also ordained women as priests.
In 1992 Maria Jepsen became the first Lutheran woman bishop in the world, in Hamburg.

abschnitte.text: With **ordination**, a person is appointed to a **spiritual office**. They may then, for example, preach, baptise and lead the Lord's Supper. In the Catholic and Orthodox churches this is called **consecration**. Whether women may also be ordained is answered differently by the churches.

abschnitte.titel: The first women pastors in Zurich
abschnitte.text: In **1918** the first women in Switzerland were ordained as pastors in **Zurich**. But they were not allowed to take on a parish post. In 1921 the Zurich cantonal government rejected their eligibility. Its reason was that **women had no right to vote**, so they could not be elected either. Only since **1963** have women in the Reformed church of the canton of Zurich been legally allowed to work fully as pastors.

In many Protestant churches, women are now naturally pastors. In **1992** **Maria Jepsen** became the first Lutheran **woman bishop** in the world, in Hamburg. In Switzerland, **Rita Famos** became the first president of the Evangelical Reformed Church of Switzerland in 2021. The **Christ Catholic Church** of Switzerland separated from Rome in the 19th century. Since **2000** it has also ordained women as priests.

In the Catholic Church only men are ordained as priests. In 1994, in the letter **“Ordinatio sacerdotalis”**, Pope **John Paul II** declared that the Church has no authority to ordain women as priests. He justified this by saying that Jesus chose only men as apostles. Many Catholics, including in Switzerland, wish for a change. Others hold to the existing teaching. The Orthodox churches also do not ordain women.

gewusst: The first two Zurich women pastors of 1918 were called Elise Pfister and Rosa Gutknecht.
In Switzerland, women's suffrage at federal level was only introduced in 1971.

teile.einleitung: The Fraumünster is a famous church in the old town of Zurich. It stands on the Limmat opposite the Grossmünster. Its coloured glass windows by Marc Chagall are known all over the world.
wichtigste: The Fraumünster stands in Zurich.
King Louis the German founded a convent for women here in 853.
The last abbess, Katharina von Zimmern, handed the convent over to the city in 1524.
In the choir there are five glass windows by Marc Chagall.
The middle Christ window is mainly green.
Augusto Giacometti created the large window in the north transept in 1945.

abschnitte.text: In the year **853**, King **Louis the German** founded a **convent for women** in Zurich. His daughter Hildegard became the first abbess. An abbess is the head of a women's convent. The convent was very powerful for a long time. The abbesses at times had important rights in Zurich, for example the right to mint coins.

In the time of the **Reformation**, much changed in Zurich. In 1524 the last abbess, **Katharina von Zimmern**, handed the convent over to the **city of Zurich**. In this way she prevented conflict and violence. The Fraumünster then became a Reformed church, and it is one to this day.

The artist **Marc Chagall** created **five** large glass windows for the choir of the Fraumünster. They were inaugurated in 1970. They show stories from the Bible. The middle one is the **Christ window**, and it glows mainly **green**. Chagall came from a **Jewish family** in Russia, in what is now Belarus. Many of his pictures show figures from the Bible.

As early as **1945** the Swiss artist **Augusto Giacometti** created the large window in the **north transept**. It is very tall and colourful. Later Chagall also designed a rose window in the south transept. Every day many visitors come to see the windows.

gewusst: Chagall was already over 80 years old when he created the windows for the Fraumünster.
Augusto Giacometti was a relative of the famous sculptor Alberto Giacometti.

teile.einleitung: Army chaplaincy looks after the spiritual concerns of soldiers. Army chaplains listen, advise and help in difficult situations. In the Swiss Army this task has existed for a very long time.
wichtigste: In the past, army chaplains in Switzerland were called field preachers.
Since 2004 they have officially been called army chaplains.
They are there for all members of the army, regardless of religion and worldview.
Army chaplains hold the rank of captain.
The conversations are confidential.
At the start of the 2020s, army chaplaincy opened up to Jewish and Muslim communities.

abschnitte.text: In **military service** many people are far away from home. Some are homesick, have worries in the family or problems on duty. Then they can turn to the **army chaplaincy**. The chaplains listen, advise and help further. The conversations are **confidential**. Army chaplaincy is an offer for everyone, from the recruit to the commander.

abschnitte.titel: From field preacher to army chaplain
abschnitte.text: In the past the chaplains in the Swiss Army were called **field preachers**. They held services and were responsible for all soldiers, regardless of denomination. With the **Army XXI** reform the name was changed in **2004**. Since then they have been called **army chaplains**. The new name stresses **pastoral care**, that is, accompanying people, rather than preaching.

Army chaplains hold the military rank of **captain**. But they stand **outside the normal chain of command**. This is important so that the soldiers can trust them. What someone says is not passed on to superiors. Army chaplaincy is there for **all members of the army**, regardless of religion and worldview.

For almost **140 years** the **national churches** alone provided army chaplaincy, that is, the Reformed, the Catholic and the Christian Catholic Church. At the start of the **2020s**, **free churches** as well as **Jewish** and **Muslim** chaplains were added. In this way army chaplaincy reflects better how diverse Switzerland is today. At the start of 2022 around **170** army chaplains were in service.

gewusst: With Army Revision 23, the number of army chaplains was meant to rise to about 240.
Many other countries also have a chaplaincy for their army.

teile.einleitung: The Inquisition was a Church court procedure against people who departed from the official teaching of the Catholic Church. It arose in the Middle Ages and in some countries lasted into the 19th century.
wichtigste: The Latin word “inquisitio” means investigation.
People who departed from Church teaching were called heretics.
Around 1231 Pope Gregory IX appointed papal inquisitors.
Many inquisitors belonged to the Dominican order.
The Spanish Inquisition arose at the end of the 15th century, and the Grand Inquisitor Tomás de Torquemada is well known.
Death sentences were carried out not by the Church but by the secular authorities.

abschnitte.text: The Latin word **inquisitio** means **investigation**. In an Inquisition a judge himself looked for suspects and evidence instead of waiting for an accusation. The aim was to find **heretics**. This was the name for people who departed from the official teaching of the Church. The aim was to get them to renounce their beliefs.

In the 12th and 13th centuries groups spread that believed differently from the Church. Particularly well known are the **Cathars** in southern France. They were heavily persecuted in the 13th century, including by military campaigns. Around **1231** Pope **Gregory IX** appointed his own papal inquisitors. Many of them belonged to the mendicant order of the **Dominicans**, some also to the Franciscans.

Suspects were questioned and often had to wait a long time for their verdict. Those who repented of their error usually received a penance, such as a pilgrimage or prison. There were also harsh means of compulsion in the interrogations. Those who did not recant could be sentenced to death. But the death sentences were carried out by the **secular authorities**, that is, princes or cities, not by the Church itself.

In 1478 a separate Inquisition arose in Spain, closely tied to the royal house. It was directed above all against baptised Jews and Muslims, who were accused of secretly holding on to their old faith. Its best-known head was the Grand Inquisitor **Tomás de Torquemada**. The verdicts were announced publicly at an **auto-da-fé**, which means “act of faith”. The Spanish Inquisition was finally abolished only in 1834.

In 1542 the Pope founded a central authority in Rome, the **Roman Inquisition**. In 1633 the scientist **Galileo Galilei** also had to answer to it. From this authority the present-day doctrinal office of the Vatican developed, which no longer imposes such punishments. Historians today study the Inquisition closely using old records. In the year 2000 the Catholic Church apologised for wrongs in its history, also in connection with the Inquisition.

gewusst: Many records of the Roman Inquisition have been accessible to researchers only since 1998.
The witch hunts in Europe were mostly carried out by secular courts, not by the Inquisition.

teile.einleitung: The Three Kings' cake belongs to 6 January, Epiphany, in Switzerland. A small figure of a king is hidden in one piece. Whoever finds it is king or queen for a day.
wichtigste: The Three Kings' cake is eaten on Epiphany, 6 January.
In one piece there is a small figure of a king, usually made of plastic.
Whoever finds the figure becomes king or queen for a day.
The cake usually comes with a golden paper crown.
The Swiss cake is made of sweet yeast dough and consists of balls like a blossom.
Max Währen made the custom well known again in the 1950s.
In France people eat the Galette des Rois.

abschnitte.text: On **6 January** Christians remember the **wise men from the East**. According to the Gospel of Matthew they followed a star to the newborn Jesus. They brought **gold, frankincense and myrrh** as gifts. Later they were called kings and given the names **Caspar, Melchior and Balthazar**. On their feast day in Switzerland, people bake or buy a Three Kings' cake.

The **Swiss Three Kings' cake** is baked from sweet **yeast dough**, like a plait loaf. Around one large **ball** in the middle lie several small balls. Together they look like a **blossom**. On top people often sprinkle **pearl sugar** and flaked almonds. Some cakes also contain raisins.

In one of the pieces of cake there is a small **figure of a king**, usually made of plastic. Everyone hopes to find it. Whoever gets the piece with the figure becomes **king or queen** for a day. He or she may put on the golden **paper crown** that comes with the cake. Often the king may then also decide something. When eating, of course, you have to bite carefully.

The custom is old, but in Switzerland it had almost been forgotten. In the **1950s** the bread researcher **Max Währen** revived it. Bakeries joined in, and soon the cake was popular all over the country. Today Swiss bakeries and shops sell very many Three Kings' cakes around 6 January.

There are cakes for Epiphany elsewhere too. In **France** people eat the **Galette des Rois**, the “cake of the kings”. In the north of France it is often made of **puff pastry** with an almond filling. In Spain the cake is called “Roscón de Reyes” and is ring-shaped. Everywhere the same applies: whoever finds the hidden figure is lucky.

gewusst: In the past, a dried bean was often hidden in the cake instead of a figure.
In French-speaking Switzerland, the Galette des Rois is also known alongside the Three Kings' cake.
